spots.name: Baldwin Street
spots.summary: Baldwin Street, in Dunedin, New Zealand, is located in the residential suburb of North East Valley, 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) northeast of Dunedin's central business district.

spots.name: The Octagon
spots.summary: The Octagon is the city centre of Dunedin, in the South Island of New Zealand. It is an eight-sided plaza with a circular one-way carriageway, bisected by the city's main street, and is also the central terminus of two other main thoroughfares.

spots.name: St Paul's Cathedral, Dunedin
spots.summary: St Paul's Cathedral is an Anglican cathedral church located in The Octagon near the Dunedin Town Hall in Dunedin, New Zealand. The cathedral is the seat of the Bishop of Dunedin and the mother church of the Anglican Diocese of Dunedin.

spots.name: Dunedin Botanic Garden
spots.summary: The Dunedin Botanic Garden is located at the northern end of central Dunedin, in the South Island of New Zealand. The garden is close to the University of Otago and one of the city's most historic cemeteries, the Northern Cemetery, on a spur of Signal Hill and on the river plain immediately below it.

spots.name: Otago Museum
spots.summary: Tūhura Otago Museum, located near the city centre of Dunedin, New Zealand, adjacent to the University of Otago campus, is one of the country's largest museums and a prominent attraction in the city.

spots.name: Dunedin Town Hall
spots.summary: The Dunedin Town Hall, also known as the Dunedin Centre, is a municipal building in the city of Dunedin in New Zealand. It is located in the heart of the city extending from The Octagon, the central plaza, to Moray Place through a whole city block.

spots.name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
spots.summary: The Dunedin Public Art Gallery holds the main public art collection of the city of Dunedin, New Zealand. Located in The Octagon in the heart of the city, it is close to the city's public library, Dunedin Town Hall, and other facilities such as the Regent Theatre.

spots.name: Castle Street
spots.summary: Castle Street is a major street in the city of Dunedin, New Zealand. The street runs in a north-north-east direction from Stuart Street outside Dunedin Railway Station to the southern end of the Dunedin Botanic Garden, and is bisected into two distinct parts by the University of Otago campus.

spots.name: Olveston

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Olveston Historic Home is a substantial house and museum in an inner suburb of Dunedin, New Zealand. The house was designed by Ernest George in the Jacobean style in the early 20th century for the Theomin family.

spots.name: New Zealand Sports Hall of Fame
spots.summary: The New Zealand Sports Hall of Fame is an organisation commemorating New Zealand's greatest sporting triumphs. It was inaugurated as part of the New Zealand sesquicentenary celebrations in 1990.
spots.wikipediaTitle: New Zealand Sports Hall of Fame

spots.name: First Church of Otago

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: First Church is a prominent church in the New Zealand city of Dunedin. It is located in the heart of the city on Moray Place, 100 metres to the south of the city centre. The church is the city's primary Presbyterian church.

spots.name: Allied Media
spots.summary: Allied Media is an independent New Zealand media and publishing company based in Dunedin. The company's main asset is the Otago Daily Times, New Zealand's oldest daily newspaper.

spots.name: Knox Church
spots.summary: Knox Church is a notable building in Dunedin, New Zealand. It houses the city's second Presbyterian congregation and is the city's largest church of any denomination.

spots.name: Toitū Otago Settlers Museum
spots.summary: The Toitū Otago Settlers Museum is a regional history museum in Dunedin, New Zealand. Its brief covers the territory of the old Otago Province, that is, New Zealand from the Waitaki River south, though its main focus is the city of Dunedin. It is New Zealand's oldest history museum.

spots.name: Regent Theatre
spots.summary: The Regent Theatre is a theatre in Dunedin, New Zealand, with a seating capacity of about 1,650. It is in The Octagon, the city's central plaza, directly opposite the Municipal Chambers and close to the Dunedin Public Art Gallery.

spots.name: Dunedin Chinese Garden
spots.summary: The Dunedin Chinese Garden is a Chinese garden located in Dunedin, New Zealand.

spots.name: Dunedin Cenotaph
spots.summary: The Cenotaph in the southern New Zealand city of Dunedin stands in the centre of Queens Gardens, close to the city centre. It is the city's main war memorial.

spots.name: Hocken Collections
spots.summary: Hocken Collections (Māori: Uare Taoka o Hākena, formerly the Hocken Library) is a research library, historical archive, and art gallery based in Dunedin, New Zealand. Its library collection, which is of national significance, is administered by the University of Otago.

photo.author: The original uploader was Grutness at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Moray Place
spots.summary: Moray Place is an octagonal street which surrounds the city centre of Dunedin, Otago, New Zealand. The street is intersected by Stuart Street, Princes Street and George Street. Like many streets in Dunedin, it is named for a street in the Scottish capital Edinburgh.

spots.name: George Street
spots.summary: George Street is the main street of Dunedin, the second largest city in the South Island of New Zealand. It runs for two and a half kilometres north-northeast from The Octagon in the city centre to the foot of Pine Hill. It is straight and undulates gently as it skirts the edge of the hills to its northwest.

spots.name: Forsyth Barr Stadium
spots.summary: Forsyth Barr Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Dunedin, New Zealand. At various stages of development it was also known as Dunedin Stadium or Awatea Street Stadium, or its non-commercial official name during the 2011 Rugby World Cup and 2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup, Otago Stadium.

spots.name: Museum of Natural Mystery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Dunedin Museum of Natural Mystery is a private museum of bones, bone art, ethnographic artifacts, and assorted curios in Dunedin, New Zealand. Created by mural artist and sculptor Bruce Mahalski, in his Royal Terrace residence, it opened to the public in March 2018.

spots.name: Former Trinity Methodist Church, Dunedin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The former Trinity Methodist Church is registered as a category I historic place by Heritage New Zealand, which recognises its historic and architectural significance. Originally a Methodist church, it is located on the corner of Moray Place and Upper Stuart Street, in the heart of the southern city of Dunedin.

spots.name: Queens Gardens
spots.summary: Queens Gardens is a roughly triangular area of trees and lawn in central Dunedin, New Zealand.

spots.name: All Saints Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: All Saints' Church is a heritage-listed Anglican church located in Dunedin, New Zealand. Established in 1865, the church is part of the Dunedin North parish in the Diocese of Dunedin.

spots.name: Cargill Monument
spots.summary: The Cargill Monument is a notable public monument in central Dunedin, New Zealand. It is dedicated to the city's founding father, Captain William Cargill, and is approximately 7.5 metres (25 ft) in height.

spots.name: Dunedin Athenaeum and Mechanics' Institute
spots.summary: Dunedin Athenaeum and Mechanics' Institute is the oldest continuously operating library in New Zealand. Established to provide education, public lectures, a space for community meetings and access to newspapers, periodicals and books.

spots.name: Stuart Memorial
spots.summary: The Stuart Memorial is a statue of clergyman Donald McNaughton Stuart located in central Dunedin, New Zealand. It sits adjacent to Queens Gardens, close to a statue of Queen Victoria. The memorial is a bronze statue of Stuart seated in a solemn pose, atop a large concrete, granite, and andesite plinth.

photo.author: Sculptor was William Leslie Morison, photo by Benchill

spots.name: Tomahawk Beach
spots.summary: Tomahawk Beach is a beach on the Pacific Ocean 7.5 kilometres (4.7 mi) southeast of the city centre of Dunedin, New Zealand.

spots.name: Bank of New Zealand Building
spots.summary: The Bank of New Zealand Building is a historic building in Dunedin, New Zealand.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Bank of New Zealand Building, Dunedin

spots.name: Dhargyey Buddhist Centre
spots.summary: Dhargyey Buddhist Centre is the headquarters of the Buddhist community in Dunedin, New Zealand, based at Linden, a Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga category 1 historic place.

spots.name: Otago Pioneer Women's Memorial Hall
spots.summary: The Otago Pioneer Women's Memorial Hall is a building in Dunedin, New Zealand, registered as a Category 1 historic place by Heritage New Zealand.

spots.name: New Zealand Insurance Company Building, Dunedin
spots.summary: The New Zealand Insurance Company Building is a historic building in Dunedin, New Zealand.
spots.wikipediaTitle: New Zealand Insurance Company Building, Dunedin

spots.name: Law Courts
spots.summary: Designed by John Campbell, the law courts are one of the finest examples of Gothic civic architecture in the country. Constructed of dark Port Chalmers breccia (commonly called bluestone) ornamented with lighter Oamaru stone the complex was completed in 1902 on the site where the city’s first prison had been located. The building is still used as Dunedin’s law courts, and comprises four courtrooms

spots.name: Dunedin Prison
spots.summary: This was the second Dunedin gaol to be built and was completed in 1898 with cells for 52 men and 20 women. It operated as both a men’s and women’s prison until 2007 when all prison services were shifted to the new Otago Corrections Facility near Milton. spots.name: Otago University
spots.summary: Has some great old buildings to wander about and see; when classes are on it's a good place to sit, people-watch and take it all in, some good food/cafes/bars are nearby too.

spots.name: Arc Cafe
spots.summary: Opened in 1997 and closed in the late 2000s, Arc Cafe was a very popular place for music, art and alternative cultures in Dunedin. You can still view its building on the street (it is now used by a bakery shop called “Body of the Year”). You can also view paintings, photos and music from their website. The website is maintained by Elliott Young, one of the original founders of Arc Cafe.

spots.name: Blue Oyster Art Project Space
spots.summary: Playfully named after the Blue Oyster gay biker bar featured in the 1984 comedy film Police Academy, this not for profit gallery run by the Blue Oyster Arts Trust began its life in 1999 and since then has been supporting experimental and innovative art practices.

spots.name: Speight's Brewery
spots.summary: Children under 15 require adult supervision. The brewery has been a Dunedin landmark since its founding in 1876. The guided tour takes you through the Speight's brewery, sharing the heritage and culture of beer, from the Babylonians to today. The tour's finale is a 25-minute beer tasting.
